newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says EU-type deal would not help Sherritt.
newsitem.headline: Canada says EU-type deal would not help Sherritt.

text.p: Sherritt International Corp would not win new relief from U.S. rules on Cuba if Canada were to match a deal that Washington reached with the European Union (EU), Trade Minister Art Eggleton said Tuesday.

He and U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat have agreed to hold further consultations, but he is not seeking the sort of agreement over Cuba announced on Friday between the EU and the United States, Eggleton told reporters.
Eggleton said one of the concessions the EU got out of Washington related to a waiver of Title 4 of the Helms-Burton Act under which executives are barred from the United States.

Executives of Canada's Sherritt International Corp may not enter the United States because Washington has deemed that the mining company is using property in Cuba that has been expropriated from Americans.
But he asserted that an arrangement that the EU has won would not benefit Canada.

"With respect to Title 4, it wouldn't apply to Canada anyway, because they're saying it isn't retroactive, so it wouldn't cover the Sherritt group, and they're also saying telling me that they're not looking at any other Canadian companies," he said.
He said U.S. President Bill Clinton had already agreed to waive another provision, Title 3, under which foreign companies using American property in Cuba can be sued.

Eggleton said that under the European agreement, the United States agreed to discuss the issue in multilateral discussions on investment under the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development.
The minister told Parliament later that if there were no progress in those talks, Canada would launch a challenge of the Helms-Burton Act under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
"If the talks stall...then we'll use it (NAFTA)," he said.

Canada had held off going to NAFTA until the results of an EU challenge at the Geneva-based World Trade Organization were known. But as part of the arrangement reached last Friday, the EU is no longer going to use the WTO.
